narrative.overview:
Simple Snip is a compact native desktop utility. Its visual character is practical, restrained, and precise: system typography, quiet preferences, familiar GPUI Kit controls, and image-first capture and pin surfaces. Controls support the image without turning annotation into a separate application frame.

This document merges the existing design guidance with the confirmed 2026-10-25 correction and the current Rust implementation. It describes GPUI Kit (0.8.0) on Windows AMD64 and macOS ARM64. The North Star is descriptive shorthand for the incumbent system; it is not a new user-selected brand identity. After unlocking, macOS checks verified inline rectangle/arrow annotation, undo/redo, below/inside toolbar placement and finish/cancel focus recovery. Remaining tools, dark theme, small images and Windows still need acceptance. Measurements remain source-observed unless explicitly verified.
keyCharacteristics: Native system typography and semantic Kit theme colors.
Compact independent geometric icons with names and tooltips.
Annotation in the screenshot overlay or existing selected pin.
A small toolbar tight against the image's lower-right edge.
Quiet preferences with descriptive rows and actionable recovery text.

rules.name: The Semantic Surface Rule
rules.body: Resolve application surfaces and control states through Kit's active semantic theme; fixed image overlays and annotation ink retain their content-specific colors.

rules.name: The Lower-Right Attachment Rule
rules.body: Align the compact toolbar with the image's lower-right edge, separated by the `image-toolbar-gap`. Place it below when the display has room; otherwise place it inside the image, above its lower border. Clamp to display bounds instead of clipping controls at the image edge.

rules.name: The One Image Surface Rule
rules.body: Edit in the current screenshot selection or original selected pin. A pin may open a toolbar-only native popup so even a tiny pin retains the complete controls; that popup must never duplicate the image canvas or become an editor application frame.

dos: **Do** keep screenshots and pins visually dominant.
**Do** attach tools to the image's lower-right edge and move them inside above the lower border when space below is unavailable.
**Do** preserve the toolbar-only native float for pins so tiny images do not crop its controls.
**Do** use semantic Kit surface/control colors and the platform system font.
**Do** keep tooltips, accessible names, keyboard access, and actionable recovery messages.
**Do** verify final toolbar placement, wrapping, focus, and dark-theme contrast in unlocked native sessions on each supported platform.
donts: **Don't** open a separate image editor window or duplicate a pin's image into a second editor frame.
**Don't** place a large application chrome, title bar, or settings sidebar around annotation.
**Don't** let the image's clipping bounds crop the toolbar.
**Don't** copy proprietary Snipaste icons or visual assets; retain the original crop-corner app icon and independent tool geometry.
**Don't** treat the sidecar's HTML previews as proof of native rendering or completed visual acceptance.
